# Introduction

The **`categorize`** analysis (Categorize Continuous Variables) provides clinicopathological researchers and biostatisticians with intuitive, publication-ready tools in jamovi and R.

## Key Capabilities

- Converts a continuous numeric variable into an ordered set of categories using equal-width intervals, sample quantiles, hand-entered break points, mean +/- SD bands, a median split, or Fisher-Jenks natural breaks. Reports the break points and the resulting category frequencies, draws the distribution with the boundaries marked, and can add the categorised variable straight to the dataset.
- Seamless integration between jamovi graphical interface and automated R syntax generation.
- Rigorous handling of missing data, small cohorts, and multi-variable stratification.

# Example Workflow in R

```r
library(ClinicoPath)

# Load package test dataset
data("categorize_test", package = "ClinicoPath", envir = environment())

# Run analysis with default settings (add the required variable arguments
# for this analysis; see ?categorize)
# ClinicoPath::categorize(
#   data = categorize_test
# )
```

# Clinical & Statistical Interpretation

Outputs generated by `categorize` include summary tables, diagnostic indicators, and high-resolution plots tailored for oncology, pathology, and clinical trial reporting.
